issues.claim: The NJ AI Hub is a 6,500-square-foot facility in West Windsor (finding 11, attributed to https://www.jerseytechandinnovation.com/p/applications-are-now-open-for-nj-ai-hub-accelerator-jan-21-deadline).
issues.problem: The number is not on the cited page. I re-opened the article (readable and raw HTML) and it describes the Hub, West Windsor, the founding partners, the co-working space and workshops, but contains no square footage. The figure is real but comes from a different source: the Plug and Play/NJ AI Hub release says the Hub 'is based in a 6,500-square-foot space in West Windsor' (prnewswire.com, 302642434); the NJEDA ribbon-cutting release I also opened does not contain the figure either.
issues.fix: Cite the Plug and Play/NJ AI Hub announcement (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nj-ai-hub-selects-plug-and-play-to-operate-its-regional-ai-accelerator-302642434.html) for the 6,500 sq ft detail, or drop the square footage since it does not affect any recommendation.

issues.claim: Data gap: 'NJ Ignite (coworking rent support of 2, 4 or 6 months) still displays on njeda.gov with no fees.'
issues.problem: Contradicted by the page it points at. https://www.njeda.gov/nj-ignite/ now states award size as rent coverage 'for a period of three months, up to 14 months or $25,000' (with tenant caps of <10 employees, <$1M trailing-12-month sales, at least one full-time NJ employee). No '2, 4 or 6 month' option appears on the current page.
issues.fix: Replace with the current published terms ('rent covered for three months, up to 14 months or $25,000') and keep the status-unknown note only for whether applications are open.

issues.claim: Finding 5's evidence block quotes the Division of Revenue fee schedule and Business.NJ.gov annual-report text under a single source_url (https://www.nj.gov/treasury/revenue/fees.shtml).
issues.problem: The fee numbers ($100 LLC certificate of formation, $75 LLC annual report, $75 corporate/LP, $30 non-profit) are on the fees page, but the annual-report quotes ('Every business in NJ must file an annual report... submitting a $75 filing fee', last day of formation month, 'can result in the revocation') are not on that page. They are on https://business.nj.gov/pages/filings-and-accounting, which the brief cites only in pitfall 6. I confirmed both pages independently; the facts are correct, the citation is incomplete.
issues.fix: Add the second URL to finding 5's evidence so each quote carries the page it came from.

issues.claim: Minor: strength ratings of High on the two vendor pages (The CoWorking Space price list; MCRCC benefits page).
issues.problem: Not wrong on the facts (I re-read both pages and the prices/member count match), but a vendor's own marketing page is primary only for its own prices; High overstates its evidential weight on anything else, and the UCEDC and NJ AI Hub entries were rated Medium for comparable vendor/newsletter material.
issues.fix: Optionally mark the coworking and chamber entries Medium for consistency, leaving the extracted prices as stated.

Rutgers-New Brunswick center serves Middlesex County, offers no in-person appointments, contact (609) 789-8364 / rutgersnb@njsbdc.com, Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30, Location and Regional Director 'TBD'.
NJSBDC Request-for-Counseling page lists TCNJ as serving Middlesex, Hunterdon, Somerset and Mercer (the county-coverage conflict flagged in caveats).

Business.NJ.gov: SCORE provides 'free, confidential, and professional business counseling'; Central Jersey SCORE covers Somerset, Hunterdon and Middlesex; Princeton SCORE covers Middlesex, Mercer, Burlington, Camden, Gloucester & Salem.
Business.NJ.gov: NJBAC helps 'all at no cost and strictly confidential'; NJSBDC help is 'free, hands-on guidance'.

NJ State Library databases free to all NJ residents with a library card: Business Source Premier 'Over 2,300 full-text journals, including more than 1,100 peer-reviewed titles'; Regional Business News '75 business journals, newspapers, and newswires'; Reference Solutions '7 Reference USA databases' (U.S. Businesses, U.S. New Businesses).
NJBAC helpline 1-800-Jersey-7 (1-800-537-7397), 'Request a Meeting With Us', Business.NJ.gov live chat with NJBAC experts, downloadable NJ Small Business Manual, mentor/online-presence referrals.
Division of Revenue fee schedule: LLC certificate of formation $100.00; LLC annual report $75.00; annual report also $75 for corporations and LPs and $30 for non-profits.

'Every business in NJ must file an annual report... submitting a $75 filing fee', due annually the last day of the formation month, business responsible even without a state notice, failure 'can result in the revocation of your business'.

Business.NJ.gov registration guide: EIN required, online application ~15 minutes with EIN issued immediately, fax ~4 days, mail 2-4 weeks; NJ-REG tax registration; Certificate of Authorization to Collect Sales Tax only if collecting sales tax; registered agent may be the owner with a New Jersey address; no fee stated for EIN, NJ-REG or the guide.

Main Street Micro Business Loan: funding 'fully subscribed', 'no longer accepting new applications'; up to $50,000, 10-year term, 2% rate, no payments/interest year one; $100 non-refundable application fee and $400 closing fee; formed at least six months, 10 or fewer FTEs, under $1.5M revenue.

NJEDA Small Business Fund: up to $500,000; one full year in operation; total revenue no more than $3 million; must provide fixed assets (real property, machinery/equipment); 'Homebased businesses are ineligible'; $300 application fee, guarantee fee up to 0.5%, closing fee 0.5%, commitment fee 0.5%, all non-refundable.

Small Business Improvement Grant: reimbursement up to 50% of costs up to $50,000; project cost minimum $5,000; must 'Rent or own and operate from facility'; 'Home-based businesses are not eligible for reimbursement for renovation or improvement projects'; wage certification of greater of $15/hour or 120% of minimum wage; $100 approval fee; rolling applications until funding exhausted.

NJ Accelerate: within six months of graduating, need NJ tax clearance, 50% of workforce working or paying taxes in NJ, 'A minimum of 2 founders/ C-suites devoting 100% of their professional time to the Company in NJ and 80% of their time in New Jersey', targeted industry including 'Information and High Technology'; $500 application fee for the Investment Benefit, all fees non-refundable.

NJ AI Hub Accelerator: MVP-and-onward companies eligible; Plug and Play runs cohorts 'for 10-12 weeks each year'; 'Space is provided for free during the program'; paid coworking after, pending availability; 'There is no equity taken'; founded by Princeton University, the State of New Jersey, Microsoft and CoreWeave; will house co-working space and workshops; located in West Windsor.
The Hub is a 6,500-square-foot facility in West Windsor.
The 6,500-square-foot figure is nevertheless accurate: 'The Hub is based in a 6,500-square-foot space in West Windsor.'

NJRIC: 'a free AI, cybersecurity, and tech accelerator backed by the SBA'; requires registered/operating in NJ, AI/Cybersecurity/IT business, 'two or more employees', 'revenues greater than $500k'; coaching/mentoring and a Kean University Center for Cybersecurity resilience assessment.

TechUnited:NJ: founders/individuals join free; free Builder tier includes member dinners and investor roundtables, weekly Ship & Run, monthly AI Demo Night, preferred pitching consideration at AI Demo Night, weekly newsletter; Innovator tier $3,000 under 50 staff, $6,000 to 250, $9,000 above.

The CoWorking Space (North Brunswick): $35/day drop-in, 10 drop-ins $140, Weekday Co-Working $175/month, 24/7 non-dedicated $250/month, 24/7 private desk cubicle $350/month, virtual mail from $25/month; free parking, printing, up to 10 conference-room hours monthly.

UCEDC microloans: 'fixed-rate (between 5.0% - 7.75%) up to six-year loans with as little as 10% down'; under two years in operation capped at $35,000, established profitable businesses up to $50,000; no prepayment penalties; eligible uses include equipment, fixtures, inventory, working capital, renovations to owned commercial real estate that houses the business.
UCEDC is a non-profit lender.

MCRCC: 'more than 700 member businesses', signature events/programs, committees, access to county elected and appointed officials, monthly newsletter and website advertising, event sponsorship; dues not published on the page (phone 732.745.8090).
Business.NJ.gov funding list renders 80 programs ('Showing 1-10 of 80 items') at the NJ Ignite funding URL.
NJ Ignite is coworking rent support for '2, 4 or 6 months' with no fees.
